rules: A caption line is not an exhibit boundary. Seven printed lines here carry two captions at once ('Figure 5: ... Figure 6: ...', 'Figure 10: ... Figure 11: ...', 'Figure 16: ... Figure 17: ...'), and on two of them the caption TEXT is interleaved word by word ('Figure 10: The relationship between total biomass Figure 11: The relationship between CoV of total Figure 12: ... and number of species'), so no single substring carries one caption and those rows are typed from the crop. [caption.verbatim]

A caption can also be blocked by typography rather than by a neighbour: Figure 16's caption hyphenates across a line ('more se-' / 'vere drought') and prints its tail below Figure 17's caption, so the verbatim has to be dehyphenated by hand and the row marked typed-from-crop. [caption.words]

The same exhibit prints as several bitmaps. Three figures here are one caption over three separately measured panels in a row (Figures 14, 23, 24, 25), so the record takes one row per panel with the printed number and caption repeated, and 'panel_count' stays 1 per row - the panel count belongs to the printed exhibit, the rows belong to the regions. [geometry.panel_count]

A dot cloud with a mean polyline is a scatter, not a line chart: Figures 10-13 and 20 print hundreds of points, one per species combination, and the polyline only joins the column means. Calling this 'line' would erase the fact that the paper shows its dispersion. The body is the only key - 'Each point in the figure represents a species combination. And straight lines connect the mean values' - because the art carries no legend for the overlay. [geometry.family]

'Legend inside' is not the same as 'legend explains the art'. Four exhibits keep a key copied from a sibling: Figures 5 and 6 key 'P.alba' under captions naming other species, Figure 8 keys one species for a plot with two band colours and no band entry, and Figures 21 and 22 print five shaded bands and five percentages with no key at all. The key's existence is measured; its accuracy is not guaranteed. [geometry.legend]

A colour ramp without a scale is not a colour bar. Five scatter panels shade their dots pale-to-dark with no strip and no ticks, so 'colorbar' records the graded ink and the note has to say the grade is unlabelled; the paper never states what the gradient measures. [geometry.colorbar]

Numeric pointers are not equally distributed: 23 of the 25 printed figures are named by number somewhere, but Figure 1 is read only as 'from the graph' and Figure 14 only as 'Figure 14 shows' inside the sentence that supplies its own caption. Two exhibits therefore carry first_page null or a self-quoting lead. [mention.first_page]

The Summary cites forward: p1 prints 'The results are shown in Figure 7.' and 'Figure 10 to 13', so the earliest mention of Figure 7 is eleven pages before the art. Lead lag is measured from the first printed mention anywhere in the paper, summary included, and a negative lead of -11 is a fact about the paper, not an error to be clamped. [mention.lead_pages]

One pointer names a range and the extractor sees only its head: 'Figure 10 to 13' is recorded against Figure 10 alone, and Figures 11, 12 and 13 then take their first mention from the body. A range pointer must not be silently expanded into four mentions. [mention.count]

Panel letters are not separate exhibits and not separate pointers: '(a) (b) (c)' print above or below each row and the caption assigns the parameter values, so Figure 25's four mentions are one bullet list naming (a), (b) and (c); the count is the number of distinct prose sentences, never the number of panel labels. [mention.style]

Placement and use disagree twice, in opposite directions: Figure 3 floats to the top of p5 above every heading there while its sentence closes 1.4 on p4, and Figures 10-13 print on p15 above nothing while their reading sentences sit in 4.1.3 on p14. Both rows take the section that reads them, and the note records the printed page. [place.section_path]

Caption side splits by kind without exception on this paper: all 25 figure captions print BELOW the art and all 3 table captions print ABOVE the grid, including the two tables whose captions are welded onto a figure caption line. [caption.position]

Two tables can be cited by number while nothing else about them is conventional: Table 1 is announced one page before it prints ('The key notations are shown in Table 1.'), Table 2 is cited twice and printed between the two citations, and Table 3's stub column prints panel letters rather than names, so it only joins to the art above it through '(a) (b) (c)'. [mention.lead_pattern]
